summary: For a coating shop storing 60 gal of unspecified flammable “solvent,” Prop 65 cannot be ruled in or out on storage quantity alone. California HSC §25249.6 is the core trigger: no person in the course of doing business may knowingly and intentionally expose an individual to a listed chemical without first giving a clear and reasonable warning. HSC §25249.10 provides important exclusions/limits, including that the chapter does not apply to exposure for which federal law governs warning in a manner that preempts state authority, to businesses employing fewer than 10 employees, and to exposures that pose no significant risk (carcinogens) or have no observable reproductive-effect level assuming exposure at 1,000 times the level in question. Therefore the next facts needed are: solvent identity/CAS and whether any constituents are on the Prop 65 list; reasonably anticipated occupational/consumer/environmental exposures from storage/coating use; facility employee count; and whether exposure is below an applicable safe-harbor level. If the solvent contains a listed chemical and a non-exempt business knowingly causes exposure above the applicable no-significant-risk/no-observable-effect threshold, a Prop 65 warning obligation is likely; otherwise not established.
title: H-HAZMAT-PROP65: California Proposition 65 warning applicability is indeterminate without chemical/exposure and business facts
